AMD.short: On November 18, 2026, AMD's board amended the company's bylaws, effective immediately. The changes add stricter procedures and disclosure rules for stockholder director nominations and proposals, let the company disregard noncompliant nominee votes, require non-white proxy cards, and update the legal forum rules.

short.AMD: Most of these articles are opinion pieces, but one real event stands out: AMD shares fell about 7.7% on Nov. 20 after Hunterbrook alleged export-control violations and supply chain risks tied to China. A law firm then announced a securities investigation over undisclosed China exposure. Opinions conflict, with some calling the short-seller claims unverified and overblown, and others pointing to a high valuation.
short.NVDA: Nearly all of these articles are opinion pieces, but they point to real events: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 revenue of about $115.8 billion, up 103%, and raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75%. Its stock then fell about 14% after CEO Jensen Huang resigned and an SEC accounting probe and a state subpoena were reported. Writers disagree on whether the strong results or the leadership and legal uncertainty matter more.
short.META: The recent articles are mostly opinion and analysis pieces, not reports of a new event. They agree Meta's revenue is growing strongly, about 26% to 27.5%, but point to pressures: margins fell from 40% to 20%, capex was $34.91B, and litigation charges reached $9.89B. Legal risk and heavy AI spending matter because they weigh on profit and cash flow.
